milestone: Daily Brief API response schema closure
scenario: The user-scoped Daily Brief endpoint declares the exact nullable envelope and item metadata it emits, and Reader consumes the generated OpenAPI response type while retaining runtime normalization for untrusted payloads.

failure_before_repair.command: cd apps/api && uv run --isolated --with-editable . --extra dev python -m pytest tests/test_briefs.py -q -k openapi_declares_typed_response
failure_before_repair.result: failed: the 200 response schema had no $ref and remained an unrestricted additionalProperties object

repair: Added BriefItemResponse, DailyBriefResponse, and nullable-but-required BriefResponse Pydantic models to the existing user-scoped route.
Added response_model=BriefResponse and normalized malformed optional generated_at/title/source/content-quality values before model validation; score risk flags are exposed as strings.
Regenerated apps/api/openapi.json and reader-web generated/schema.ts so the operation now references components.schemas.BriefResponse and its nested item fields.
Replaced the Reader adapter's duplicate wire aliases with generated component types while keeping its unknown-payload guard and malformed-row filtering at the runtime boundary.

validation.command: cd apps/api && uv run --isolated --with-editable . --extra dev python -m pytest tests/test_briefs.py -q
cd apps/api && uv run --isolated --with-editable . --extra dev python -m pytest tests -q
validation.result: pass: 225 tests, 1 skipped, 4 existing SQLite deprecation warnings

validation.command: cd apps/api && uv run --isolated --with-editable . --extra dev ruff check .
cd apps/reader-web && npm test && npm run build
validation.result: pass: Reader Node suite and Next.js production build/TypeScript check

validation.command: uv run --isolated --with-editable . --extra dev python -m app.export_openapi --out openapi.json && npx --yes openapi-typescript@7.13.0 apps/api/openapi.json -o apps/reader-web/src/lib/api/generated/schema.ts
validation.result: pass: OpenAPI export and generated TypeScript completed

known_limit: This closes the local FastAPI/OpenAPI/generated-TypeScript contract only. It does not prove real PostgreSQL/provider behavior, worker materialization ownership, staging/production auth/cache, or deployed schema artifact delivery; runtime adapter normalization remains intentionally defensive because network JSON is still untrusted.
